title: The rundown
note: What's going on right now, in one place. The ↗ links out to the original source; the item's own text turns into a link only once it becomes a full entry here.

items.text: Russia told the WHO on October 6 that medical observation has ended for all roughly 200 contacts of lab worker Darya Shipilova, who died October 2 after reportedly breaking a test tube at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, with every contact testing negative — even as Russian media reported a second plague death that day, which federal health authorities deny.

UK Maritime Trade Operations logged nine attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz in the first six days of October alone — already half of September's combined total for the strait and the wider Persian Gulf — including five incidents on October 6, four of them tanker strikes, plus an Iranian Revolutionary Guard boarding that forced one tanker to turn back.

The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,818.93 Tuesday (+0.58%) and the Nasdaq at a record 27,599.79 (+0.45%), while the Dow added 253 points (+0.49%) to 51,521.28, as Treasury yields eased from multi-year highs and Nvidia's market value pushed toward $6 trillion.

France's 10-year bond yield hit 4.99% Friday, pushing its spread over German Bunds past 158 basis points — the widest since 2011 — just as Spain's Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for November 29 after a fragmented parliament rejected his housing decrees, sending the euro to a 17-month low against the dollar.

Bitcoin slid below $84,000 Wednesday morning, down from Tuesday's roughly $85,546 open, as the same oil-price spike tied to the Hormuz tanker attacks helped trigger a fresh wave of leveraged crypto liquidations.

Microsoft holds its first major Windows event in over two years today in San Francisco, where CEO Satya Nadella and Nvidia's Jensen Huang are set to detail pricing and availability for Nvidia's new RTX Spark superchip and the AI-focused Surface Laptop Ultra and Surface RTX Spark Dev Box.

The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Henri Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan), splitting the $1.2 million award for discoveries in asymmetric autocatalysis that solved a century-old puzzle about how chemistry produces molecules of a single handedness, or "homochirality."

South Korea launched the fifth Nuri rocket today from the Naro Space Center carrying a record 15 satellites — five KAIST-built cluster satellites plus ten university and research CubeSats — the country's first deployment of a satellite constellation in a single mission.

The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Karl Deisseroth (Stanford), Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel (both Germany) for discovering light-gated ion channels and turning them into optogenetics, the technique researchers now use to switch individual brain cells on and off with light.
